name: Jay-Z
hook: A Brooklyn rapper who sold his own CDs from his car, started his own label, and turned a young Chicago producer's sped-up soul samples into the sound of 'The Blueprint'.

blurb.age13: Shawn Carter, Jay-Z, was born in Brooklyn in 1969 and grew up in the Marcy Houses, a public housing project. In the early 1990s he appeared on stage with Big Daddy Kane. When no big label would sign him, he sold CDs from his car and in 1995 started his own label, Roc-A-Fella Records, with Damon Dash and Kareem Burke. His first album, 'Reasonable Doubt' (1996), had beats by DJ Premier. 'The Blueprint' (2001) was built largely on old soul records sped up and pitched higher by a young producer called Kanye West. That year he started a rap feud with Nas, which Nas answered with 'Ether'. They later made up and recorded together. He went on to run Def Jam, the label Rick Rubin had co-founded.
blurb.adult: Born in Brooklyn on 4 December 1969 and raised in the Marcy Houses. He appears on Big Daddy Kane's 'Show and Prove' (1994) and is often described as Kane's hype man in the period, which Kane has corrected: he says Jay-Z made cameo appearances on his shows. Without a major-label deal, he sold CDs from his car and founded Roc-A-Fella with Damon Dash and Kareem Burke in 1995. 'Reasonable Doubt' (1996) had production by DJ Premier, Ski and Clark Kent, and a guest verse from the Notorious B.I.G. Timbaland produced 'Big Pimpin'' (1999). 'The Blueprint' (2001), with four tracks by Kanye West, debuted at number one and is credited with making West's name. His 'Takeover', performed at Summer Jam 2001 and released on 'The Blueprint', attacked Nas and Mobb Deep; Nas answered with 'Ether' that December, and the two later reconciled and recorded together from 2006. He was president of Def Jam from 2004 to the end of 2007.
